soviet-cuisine.name: Soviet cuisine
soviet-cuisine.summary: The shared cuisine that emerged across the Soviet Union, blending national dishes with simplified French, Russian and other Eastern Bloc cooking for canteens and households.

chernozem.name: Chernozem
chernozem.summary: A very fertile, humus-rich black soil, also called black earth, found across the steppes of Ukraine and Russia, the American and Canadian plains, and South America's Pampas.

ph-m-nh-t-v-ng.name: Phạm Nhật Vượng
ph-m-nh-t-v-ng.summary: A Vietnamese property developer born in 1968, Vietnam's first US-dollar billionaire, founder of the conglomerate Vingroup, and creator of the Mivina instant noodle brand in Ukraine.

chebureki.name: Chebureki
chebureki.summary: Deep-fried turnovers filled with minced meat and onions, the national dish of Crimean Tatar cuisine and a popular street food across Eastern Europe and Central Asia.

koryo-saram-cuisine.name: Koryo-saram cuisine
koryo-saram-cuisine.summary: Distinct style of cooking descended from Korean cuisine and shaped by the countries the Koryo-saram lived in; popular across the former Soviet Union but virtually unknown in South Korea.

morkovcha.name: Morkovcha
morkovcha.summary: A spicy marinated carrot salad from Koryo-saram cuisine, the food of ethnic Koreans of the former Soviet Union.

svitoch.name: Svitoch
svitoch.summary: A Lviv-based Ukrainian confectionery manufacturer that produces chocolate and candy, owned by Nestlé since 1998.

volyn-oblast.name: Volyn Oblast
volyn-oblast.summary: A province in northwestern Ukraine bordering Poland and Belarus, with its administrative centre at Lutsk and a population of about one million.

vilnius-pink-soup-fest.name: Vilnius Pink Soup Fest
vilnius-pink-soup-fest.summary: An annual festival in Vilnius, Lithuania, celebrating šaltibarščiai, the cold beetroot soup considered a national dish, with the city decorated in pink and visitors encouraged to dress the same way.

b-rek.name: Börek
b-rek.summary: A family of thin, flaky pastries filled with meat, cheese, spinach or potatoes, popular across West Asia and Southeast Europe and often served with yogurt.

socialist-realism.name: Socialist realism
socialist-realism.summary: The official art style of the Soviet Union and other socialist states, using idealized, photorealistic scenes to advance the socialist cause; proclaimed doctrine in 1934.

kazimir-malevich.name: Kazimir Malevich
kazimir-malevich.summary: A Russian avant-garde artist who founded Suprematism, a radically abstract style of geometric painting, in 1915.

suprematism.name: Suprematism
suprematism.summary: An early 20th-century abstract art movement founded by Kazimir Malevich in 1913, based on simple geometric forms and a limited color range rather than realistic depiction.

mikhail-larionov.name: Mikhail Larionov
mikhail-larionov.summary: Russian avant-garde painter (1881–1964) who pioneered abstract Russian art, co-founded the Knave of Diamonds and Donkey's Tail groups, and worked with Sergei Diaghilev's Ballets Russes alongside his partner Natalia Goncharova.

khreshchatyk.name: Khreshchatyk
khreshchatyk.summary: The main street of Kyiv, Ukraine, running about 1.2 km from European Square to Bessarabska Square; it was destroyed by retreating Soviet troops in World War II and rebuilt afterward.

stalinist-architecture.name: Stalinist architecture
stalinist-architecture.summary: A monumental architectural style in the USSR and Eastern Bloc from the mid-1930s to mid-1950s, combining classicism, baroque, and art deco to express Soviet triumph.

artists-union-of-the-ussr.name: Artists' Union of the USSR
artists-union-of-the-ussr.summary: Soviet creative union of artists and art critics, begun in Moscow and Leningrad in 1932 and made a single national body in 1957, disbanded in 1992.

mykhailo-dzyndra.name: Mykhailo Dzyndra
mykhailo-dzyndra.summary: A Ukrainian sculptor (1921–2006) known for blending Ukrainian cultural symbolism with modernism, who spent most of his career in the United States before returning to Ukraine.

maidan-nezalezhnosti.name: Maidan Nezalezhnosti
maidan-nezalezhnosti.summary: Central square of Kyiv, Ukraine, and traditional site of major protests, including the 2004 Orange Revolution and the 2013-14 Euromaidan.

russian-provisional-government.name: Russian Provisional Government
russian-provisional-government.summary: A caretaker government formed after Nicholas II's abdication in March 1917, led first by Prince Georgy Lvov and then Alexander Kerensky, until the Bolsheviks overthrew it that October.

october-revolution.name: October Revolution
october-revolution.summary: The 1917 Bolshevik-led uprising in Petrograd that overthrew Russia's Provisional Government, following the earlier February Revolution, and triggered the Russian Civil War.

russian-soviet-federative-socialist-repu.name: Russian SFSR
russian-soviet-federative-socialist-repu.summary: The largest constituent republic of the Soviet Union from 1922 to 1991, proclaimed in 1917 after the October Revolution as the world's first communist state, capital Moscow.

viktor-yanukovych.name: Viktor Yanukovych
viktor-yanukovych.summary: Ukraine's fourth president, serving 2010 to 2014, and earlier prime minister several times; his removal in the 2014 Revolution of Dignity followed months of protest, and he has since lived in exile in Russia.

donbas.name: Donbas
donbas.summary: A historically important coal-mining region on the Russia–Ukraine border, mainly comprising Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, now largely occupied by Russia amid the Russo-Ukrainian war.

vladimir-lenin.name: Vladimir Lenin
vladimir-lenin.summary: Russian revolutionary and political theorist (1870–1924) who led the Bolsheviks and became the first head of government of Soviet Russia, then the Soviet Union, developing Marxism into Leninism.

alexander-kolchak.name: Alexander Kolchak
alexander-kolchak.summary: A Russian navy officer and polar explorer (1874–1920) who led the White movement in the Russian Civil War and briefly ruled as Supreme Ruler of Russia from 1918.

white-movement.name: White movement
white-movement.summary: The main anti-Bolshevik faction of the Russian Civil War (1917-1922), led largely by conservative officers of the former Russian Empire and united under Alexander Kolchak from 1918.

serhii-plokhy.name: Serhii Plokhy
serhii-plokhy.summary: Historian and author, born 1957, who serves as professor of Ukrainian history at Harvard University.

paul-d-anieri.name: Paul D'Anieri
paul-d-anieri.summary: American political scientist and former university administrator specializing in politics and international relations in the former Soviet Union, particularly Ukraine and Russia.

ukrainian-war-of-independence.name: Ukrainian War of Independence
ukrainian-war-of-independence.summary: A conflict fought from March 1917 to November 1921, part of the wider Russian Civil War, among Ukrainian nationalists, anarchists, German/Austro-Hungarian forces, White Russians, and Polish forces.

volunteer-army.name: Volunteer Army
volunteer-army.summary: A White Army force active in South Russia during the 1917-1920 Russian Civil War, fighting Bolsheviks and becoming the largest White movement force until merging with Wrangel's army in 1920.

ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic.name: Ukrainian SSR
ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic.summary: A constituent republic of the Soviet Union from 1922 to 1991, governed by the Communist Party of Ukraine, formed after Bolshevik forces defeated the independent Ukrainian People's Republic.

second-polish-republic.name: Second Polish Republic
second-polish-republic.summary: The Polish state existing from 1918 to 1939, ending when Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union invaded, marking the start of World War II in Europe.

mikhail-artemyevich-muravyov.name: Mikhail Muravyov
mikhail-artemyevich-muravyov.summary: Russian officer (1880–1918) who switched sides in the Russian Civil War, leading Red Guard forces that captured Kyiv in January 1918 and carried out mass terror there before rebelling against the Bolsheviks and being killed.

central-rada.name: Central Rada
central-rada.summary: The revolutionary council that governed the Ukrainian People's Republic from 1917, acting as its parliament until it was overthrown by Bolshevik forces during the Ukrainian-Soviet War.

krasnodar.name: Yekaterinodar
krasnodar.summary: Former name (until 1920) of Krasnodar, a city on the Kuban River in southern Russia founded in 1793 as a Cossack fortress.

armavir-russia.name: Armavir
armavir-russia.summary: City in Krasnodar Krai, Russia, on the Kuban River, with a population of about 187,000 and the region's second-largest industrial center.

stavropol.name: Stavropol
stavropol.summary: A city in the North Caucasus region of southern Russia, administrative centre of Stavropol Krai, called Voroshilovsk from 1935 to 1943.

dagestan.name: Dagestan
dagestan.summary: A republic of Russia in the North Caucasus along the Caspian Sea, sharing borders with Azerbaijan, Georgia and several Russian republics; one of Russia's most ethnically and linguistically diverse regions.

tuva.name: Tuva
tuva.summary: A republic of Russia in southern Siberia, at the geographic center of Asia, historically controlled by Chinese dynasties and nomadic khanates before being annexed by the Soviet Union in 1944.

buryatia.name: Buryatia
buryatia.summary: A republic of Russia in Siberia around Lake Baikal, home to the indigenous Buryats, with its capital at Ulan-Ude.

aleksandr-solzhenitsyn.name: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
aleksandr-solzhenitsyn.summary: Soviet and Russian author and dissident (1918–2008) who exposed Soviet political repression and the Gulag system, winning the 1970 Nobel Prize in Literature.

joseph-brodsky.name: Joseph Brodsky
joseph-brodsky.summary: Russian-American poet and essayist expelled from the Soviet Union in 1972, who won the 1987 Nobel Prize in Literature and became U.S. Poet Laureate.

perestroika.name: Perestroika
perestroika.summary: A late-1980s Soviet reform movement under Mikhail Gorbachev meant to restructure the economy and make socialism more efficient, amid growing stagnation and unrest.

samizdat.name: Samizdat
samizdat.summary: A form of dissident activity in the Soviet-era Eastern Bloc in which banned texts were manually copied and passed from reader to reader to evade censorship.

chinghiz-aitmatov.name: Chinghiz Aitmatov
chinghiz-aitmatov.summary: A Kyrgyz author (1928-2008) who wrote mainly in Russian as well as Kyrgyz, regarded as one of the best-known figures in Kyrgyz literature.

vasil-byka.name: Vasil Bykaŭ
vasil-byka.summary: Belarusian author (1924-2003) known for novels and novellas about World War II, nominated for the Nobel Prize in Literature by figures including Joseph Brodsky.

rasul-gamzatov.name: Rasul Gamzatov
rasul-gamzatov.summary: Soviet and Russian poet (1923–2003) who wrote in the Avar language, best known for the poem Zhuravli, which became a famous Soviet song.

ukrainian-people-s-republic.name: Ukrainian People's Republic
ukrainian-people-s-republic.summary: A short-lived state proclaimed in late 1917 after the Bolshevik seizure of power, covering much of central Ukraine before its territory was absorbed in the Ukrainian War of Independence.

sixtiers.name: Sixtiers
sixtiers.summary: A generation of young Ukrainians in the late 1950s and 1960s who revived Ukrainian literature and national feeling, many later persecuted by Soviet authorities.

volodymyr-vladko.name: Volodymyr Vladko
volodymyr-vladko.summary: A Soviet Ukrainian fiction writer, journalist, and theatre critic (1901-1974), and a member of the Union of Soviet Writers from 1934.

yury-dombrovsky.name: Yury Dombrovsky
yury-dombrovsky.summary: Russian writer (1909–1978) who spent nearly eighteen years in Soviet prison camps and exile.

the-faculty-of-useless-knowledge.name: The Faculty of Useless Knowledge
the-faculty-of-useless-knowledge.summary: Novel by Yury Dombrovsky about the fate of the Russian intelligentsia during the Great Purge, written 1964–1975; its 1975 publication in Paris is said to have caused his death.

venedikt-yerofeyev.name: Venedikt Yerofeyev
venedikt-yerofeyev.summary: Russian writer and Soviet dissident, born in 1938 near Kandalaksha and died in 1990 in Moscow.

oleg-grigoriev.name: Oleg Grigoriev
oleg-grigoriev.summary: Russian poet and artist (1943–1992) regarded as a successor to the Oberiu literary tradition; many of his short poems became modern folklore.

oles-berdnyk.name: Oles Berdnyk
oles-berdnyk.summary: Ukrainian science fiction writer, philosopher and Soviet-era dissident (1926–2003) who wrote over 20 novels and was imprisoned after founding the Ukrainian Helsinki Group.

igor-rosokhovatski.name: Ihor Rosokhovatskyi
igor-rosokhovatski.summary: A Ukrainian writer who lived from 1929 to 2015.

old-church-slavonic.name: Old Church Slavonic
old-church-slavonic.summary: The first Slavic literary language, standardized by 9th-century missionaries Cyril and Methodius for translating scripture, and ancestor of the liturgical Church Slavonic still used today.

eurocon.name: Eurocon
eurocon.summary: An annual European science fiction convention, first held in Trieste in 1972, whose host committee is chosen each year by vote and which awards the European SF Awards.

alexander-friedmann.name: Alexander Friedmann
alexander-friedmann.summary: A Russian and Soviet physicist and mathematician (1888-1925) who first proposed that the universe is expanding, formulating the Friedmann equations that underpin the theory.

george-gamow.name: George Gamow
george-gamow.summary: Soviet and American physicist and cosmologist (1904–1968) who advanced the Big Bang theory, explained alpha decay through quantum tunneling, and predicted the cosmic microwave background radiation.

russian-cosmism.name: Russian cosmism
russian-cosmism.summary: A late 19th- and early 20th-century Russian movement blending science, religion and metaphysics, holding that humanity could achieve immortality and a cosmic destiny through technology.

dmitri-ivanenko.name: Dmitri Ivanenko
dmitri-ivanenko.summary: Soviet theoretical physicist of Ukrainian origin (1904–1994) who contributed to nuclear physics, field theory and gravitation theory, led theoretical physics departments in Kharkiv, and was a professor at Moscow State University.

konstantin-tsiolkovsky.name: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky
konstantin-tsiolkovsky.summary: Russian scientist (1857–1935) considered a founding father of modern rocketry and astronautics, whose work later inspired Wernher von Braun and Soviet rocket engineers; lived as a recluse near Kaluga, southwest of Moscow.

jules-verne.name: Jules Verne
jules-verne.summary: French novelist, poet and playwright, 1828 to 1905, whose adventure novels such as Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas made him one of the most translated authors ever.

h-g-wells.name: H. G. Wells
h-g-wells.summary: English writer (1866–1946) of more than forty novels, often called the 'father of science fiction' for works like The Time Machine that imagined time travel and alien invasion.

alexander-bogdanov.name: Alexander Bogdanov
alexander-bogdanov.summary: A Russian and Soviet physician, philosopher and Bolshevik revolutionary (1873-1928) who pioneered blood transfusion and systems theory, and was a rival of Lenin within the early Bolshevik party.

gleb-kotelnikov.name: Gleb Kotelnikov
gleb-kotelnikov.summary: Russian and Soviet inventor (1872-1944) who created the knapsack parachute and the braking parachute.

laika.name: Laika
laika.summary: A stray Moscow dog who became the first animal to orbit Earth, aboard the Soviet Sputnik 2 spacecraft in 1957, dying from overheating hours into the flight.

sputnik-2.name: Sputnik 2
sputnik-2.summary: The second Soviet satellite, launched on 3 November 1957, carrying the dog Laika as the first animal to reach orbit.

zond-5.name: Zond 5
zond-5.summary: A Soviet spacecraft that circled the Moon in September 1968 carrying two tortoises and other organisms, the first Moon mission with animals to return safely to Earth.

vladimir-vernadsky.name: Vladimir Vernadsky
vladimir-vernadsky.summary: Russian, Ukrainian and Soviet mineralogist and geochemist (1863–1945), a founder of geochemistry and biogeochemistry, known for his 1926 book popularizing the concept of the biosphere.

noosphere.name: Noosphere
noosphere.summary: A philosophical concept, developed by Vladimir Vernadsky and Pierre Teilhard de Chardin, describing a planetary 'sphere of reason' formed by human thought as the next stage of the biosphere.

alexander-chizhevsky.name: Alexander Chizhevsky
alexander-chizhevsky.summary: A Soviet interdisciplinary scientist (1897-1964) who founded heliobiology, the study of the sun's effects on biology, and used historical data to link solar cycles with climate and human activity.

global-innovation-index.name: Global Innovation Index
global-innovation-index.summary: An annual ranking of countries by their capacity for innovation, published since 2007 by the World Intellectual Property Organization using data from sources such as the World Bank.

list-of-minor-planets-3001-4000.name: 3113 Chizhevskij
list-of-minor-planets-3001-4000.summary: A numbered minor planet within this catalogue's 3001 to 4000 range, tracked using orbital data from JPL's Small-Body Database and the Minor Planet Center.

nikolai-chernykh.name: Nikolai Chernykh
nikolai-chernykh.summary: Soviet astronomer (1931–2004) who discovered minor planets and comets at the Crimean Astrophysical Observatory.

russian-academy-of-sciences.name: Russian Academy of Sciences
russian-academy-of-sciences.summary: Russia's national academy of sciences, established by Peter the Great in 1724 as the St. Petersburg Academy of Sciences with guidance from Gottfried Leibniz, now headquartered in Moscow.

georgy-flerov.name: Georgy Flerov
georgy-flerov.summary: Soviet physicist (1913-1990) who discovered spontaneous fission and wrote to Stalin urging a Soviet nuclear weapons program; element 114, flerovium, is named after his research lab.

joseph-stalin.name: Joseph Stalin
joseph-stalin.summary: Soviet politician who ruled the Soviet Union from 1922 until his death in 1953, becoming its de facto dictator by the 1930s and formalizing Marxism–Leninism.

nicholas-ii.name: Nicholas II
nicholas-ii.summary: Last emperor of Russia, reigning from 1894 until his 1917 abdication ended the Romanov dynasty; he and his family were killed in 1918.

bolsheviks.name: Bolsheviks
bolsheviks.summary: A radical Marxist faction led by Vladimir Lenin that split from the Mensheviks in 1903, seized power in Russia's October Revolution of 1917, and later became the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.

south-caucasus.name: Transcaucasia
south-caucasus.summary: Also called the South Caucasus, a region on the southern Caucasus Mountains roughly matching modern Armenia, Georgia and Azerbaijan.

house-of-romanov.name: House of Romanov
house-of-romanov.summary: The imperial house of Russia from 1613 until 1917, beginning with the election of Michael Romanov as tsar and ending with the execution of Nicholas II's family in 1918.

christopher-clark.name: Christopher Clark
christopher-clark.summary: Australian historian, born 1960, based in Britain and Germany; Regius Professor of History at Cambridge, knighted in 2015 for services to Anglo-German relations.

july-crisis.name: July Crisis
july-crisis.summary: The chain of diplomatic and military escalations among European powers in mid-1914, beginning with the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, that led to the outbreak of World War I.

kalmyks.name: Kalmyks
kalmyks.summary: A Mongolic people in Europe descended from Oirats who migrated from Dzungaria in early modern times and founded the Kalmyk Khanate in the 17th century; Europe's only traditionally Buddhist ethnic group.

karelo-finnish-soviet-socialist-republic.name: Karelo-Finnish SSR
karelo-finnish-soviet-socialist-republic.summary: A republic of the Soviet Union from 1940 to 1956, when it became part of the Russian SFSR as the Karelian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic.

karelian-autonomous-soviet-socialist-rep.name: Karelian ASSR
karelian-autonomous-soviet-socialist-rep.summary: An autonomous republic of the Russian SFSR within the Soviet Union, capital Petrozavodsk, existing 1923-1940 and 1956-1991 before becoming the Republic of Karelia.

vladimir-putin.name: Vladimir Putin
vladimir-putin.summary: Russian politician and former KGB officer (born 1952) who has served as President of Russia since 2012, having also served from 2000 to 2008 and twice as Prime Minister.

napoleon.name: Napoleon
napoleon.summary: French emperor from 1804 to 1814, and briefly in 1815, who rose to power as a general during the French Revolution and led sweeping military campaigns across Europe and the Middle East.

grand-duke-dmitri-pavlovich-of-russia.name: Grand Duke Dmitri Pavlovich
grand-duke-dmitri-pavlovich-of-russia.summary: A grandson of Tsar Alexander II and first cousin of Tsar Nicholas II, raised largely at the Russian imperial court and an Olympic equestrian in 1912.
grand-duke-dmitri-pavlovich-of-russia.source_title: Grand Duke Dmitri Pavlovich of Russia

evgeny-ukhnalev.name: Yevgeny Ukhnalyov
evgeny-ukhnalev.summary: Russian artist (1931–2015) and founding member of the Russian Guild of Heraldic Artists who designed Russia's modern coat of arms and other state symbols.

gustav-shpet.name: Gustav Shpet
gustav-shpet.summary: A Russian philosopher, historian of philosophy and psychologist (1879–1937) who introduced Husserl's phenomenology to Russia and served as vice president of the Russian State Academy of Arts in Moscow.

semyon-frank.name: Semyon Frank
semyon-frank.summary: A Russian philosopher, 1877 to 1950, born Jewish, who converted to Orthodox Christianity in 1912, was expelled from Soviet Russia in 1922, lived in Berlin, then moved to Britain in 1945.

ivan-ilyin.name: Ivan Ilyin
ivan-ilyin.summary: Russian jurist and far-right political philosopher (1883–1954) who opposed the Bolshevik regime as a white émigré and was for a time sympathetic to Italian fascism.

michael-allen-gillespie.name: M. A. Gillespie
michael-allen-gillespie.summary: An American philosopher and professor at Duke University, born in 1951, who writes on political philosophy, the history of philosophy, and links between religion and modern political thought.

thomas-j-j-altizer.name: Thomas J. J. Altizer
thomas-j-j-altizer.summary: An American theologian (1927–2018) known for Death of God theology, blending Hegelian philosophy with William Blake's visionary thought.

under-the-banner-of-marxism.name: Under the Banner of Marxism
under-the-banner-of-marxism.summary: Soviet philosophical and socio-economic journal published in Moscow from 1922 to 1944. It appeared monthly, except for 1933 to 1935, when it came out every two months.

nikolai-fyodorov-philosopher.name: Nikolai Fyodorov
nikolai-fyodorov-philosopher.summary: Russian religious philosopher (1829–1903) who founded Russian cosmism, advocating scientific resurrection of the dead and physical immortality; influenced Tsiolkovsky and Scriabin.

panpsychism.name: Panpsychism
panpsychism.summary: A philosophical view, one of the oldest in philosophy of mind, holding that consciousness is a fundamental feature present throughout all matter and reality.

leon-trotsky.name: Leon Trotsky
leon-trotsky.summary: A Russian revolutionary and Soviet politician (1879–1940), a key figure alongside Lenin in the Soviet state from 1917, including the October Revolution and Civil War, later exiled in 1929 and assassinated in 1940.

trotskyism.name: Trotskyism
trotskyism.summary: A branch of Marxism and Leninism developed by Leon Trotsky in exile, which attacked Stalin's doctrine of 'Socialism in One Country' as incompatible with revolutionary ideology.

socialism-in-one-country.name: Socialism in One Country
socialism-in-one-country.summary: A Soviet policy, championed by Stalin from 1924, of building socialism within the USSR alone rather than through world revolution, opposed by Trotsky.

anatoly-lunacharsky.name: Anatoly Lunacharsky
anatoly-lunacharsky.summary: Russian Marxist revolutionary and the first Soviet People's Commissar of Education, also active throughout his career as a playwright, critic and essayist.

philosophers-ships.name: Philosophers' ships
philosophers-ships.summary: Steamships that transported over 200 intellectuals expelled from Soviet Russia to Germany in 1922.

the-revolution-betrayed.name: The Revolution Betrayed
the-revolution-betrayed.summary: 1936 book by exiled Soviet leader Leon Trotsky criticizing the Soviet Union's direction after Lenin's death, arguing Stalin's totalitarianism had undermined the revolution's promise.

great-purge.name: Great Purge
great-purge.summary: A political purge in the Soviet Union from 1936 to 1938 under Joseph Stalin, carried out mainly by the NKVD through show trials, executions and imprisonments of top party and military figures.

stalinism.name: Stalinism
stalinism.summary: The totalitarian system of government and Marxist–Leninist policies imposed by Joseph Stalin in the Soviet Union from 1927 to 1953, marked by a police state, forced collectivization, and mass repression.

georgi-plekhanov.name: Georgi Plekhanov
georgi-plekhanov.summary: Russian Marxist theorist and revolutionary (1856-1918), regarded as the father of Russian Marxism, who founded the first Russian Marxist political organization in 1883.

nikolay-chernyshevsky.name: Nikolay Chernyshevsky
nikolay-chernyshevsky.summary: Russian literary and social critic, journalist and socialist philosopher (1828–1889), the dominant intellectual figure of Russia's 1860s revolutionary democratic movement despite years of exile in Siberia.

abram-deborin.name: Abram Deborin
abram-deborin.summary: Soviet Marxist philosopher and academician (1881–1963) who moved between Bolshevik and Menshevik factions before a long career as a philosopher under Soviet rule.

vladimir-adoratsky.name: Vladimir Adoratsky
vladimir-adoratsky.summary: Russian revolutionary, Soviet historian and Marxist philosopher (1878–1945).

samovar.name: Samovar
samovar.summary: A metal container, originating in Russia, traditionally used to heat water for making tea, historically fueled by coal or kindling.

valeri-kharlamov.name: Valeri Kharlamov
valeri-kharlamov.summary: Soviet ice hockey forward (1948-1981) for CSKA Moscow, considered one of the greatest players of all time and part of a famous scoring line.

sergei-makarov-ice-hockey.name: Sergei Makarov
sergei-makarov-ice-hockey.summary: Russian former professional ice hockey right wing, part of the famed KLM Line, who won Olympic gold in 1984 and 1988 and was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame.

viacheslav-fetisov.name: Viacheslav Fetisov
viacheslav-fetisov.summary: A Russian former ice hockey defenceman, coach and politician who won two Stanley Cups with Detroit, two Olympic golds, and helped open the way for Soviet players to join the NHL.

vladislav-tretiak.name: Vladislav Tretiak
vladislav-tretiak.summary: Russian former ice hockey goaltender (born 1952) for the Soviet national team, inducted into the IIHF Hall of Fame and named to its Centennial All-Star Team as one of the sport's greatest goaltenders.

melitopol.name: Melitopol
melitopol.summary: A city in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, southeastern Ukraine, historically a key rail and road gateway to Crimea; it has been under Russian occupation since 2022.

kontinental-hockey-league.name: Kontinental Hockey League
kontinental-hockey-league.summary: International professional ice hockey league founded in 2008, made up mostly of Russian clubs and seen as a rival to the NHL; its champion wins the Gagarin Cup.

eastern_europe_russia-modern-art-005: Moscow and Leningrad Union of Artists
